fallback.text: A by-law of 1958 forbids vehicles in the park. A car, an ambulance and a tank on a plinth are all vehicles, and in everyday speech so is a bicycle, but the by-law means motor vehicles only, and that narrower reading wins. A later, more specific rule lets a vehicle on an emergency call enter, so it beats the ban. A war memorial is an exception written into the ban itself, so the ban gives way. The picture shows each rule as a dot: green where it fires, red where it applies but is defeated, grey where it does not apply. Arrows run from a stronger rule to the weaker one it beats. This is H. L. A. Hart's example (1958), worked as defeasible logic.
